headline: Take-Two surges 6% on GTA 6 hype, RBA holds rates at 4.35% with a hawkish warning, and the ASX 200 closes up 0.54% — a mixed but broadly positive day.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Massive jump last night after investment bank Piper Sandler put out a bullish note on GTA 6, and Take-Two's CEO publicly reaffirmed the game is still on track for release this year. With gamers circling 23 June as a key date, anticipation is building fast — and the market loves it.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google edged higher last night, likely buoyed by its prominent seat at the G7 AI summit alongside OpenAI and Anthropic. Analyst price targets also remain well above current levels, suggesting the market still sees upside.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped last night, dragged down by the broader NASDAQ sell-off. A Seeking Alpha analysis also raised concerns that Microsoft's cash flow doesn't quite justify its current valuation — some profit-taking followed.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced strongly today as lithium sentiment improved — spodumene (the raw lithium mineral Pilbara mines) prices are tightening globally, and solid-state battery demand forecasts are lifting the sector. A good day for the ASX lithium patch broadly.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: A quiet positive session for VDHG, which tracks a diversified mix of global and Australian shares. The ASX 200 was up 0.54% today, lifting the local portion of the fund.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped today as oil prices fell. A US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough has banks slashing their oil price forecasts — Goldman Sachs and others see less upside for crude, which weighs directly on global energy stocks like those inside this ETF.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI dipped slightly today despite positive AI news flow. The broader NASDAQ sold off last night and that sentiment carried into the ASX session for tech-heavy ETFs. Still, the underlying AI thematic remains very much intact.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Small dip for VGE today. Emerging markets are sensitive to a stronger US dollar and any global risk-off mood — neither was dramatic today, so this is just minor noise.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down today, reflecting last night's US market weakness where the S&P 500 fell 0.57% and the NASDAQ dropped 1.15%. The ASX-listed version prices off the US session, so last night's dip flowed through.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 on track — hold and watch 23 June
watch_today.detail: Take-Two jumped 6.35% last night after Piper Sandler's bullish GTA 6 note and CEO confirmation the game releases in 2026. Gamers are marking 23 June as a big date (potentially a trailer or release announcement). Your position is now just in the black (+0.27% overall). The hype is real but so is the risk — if anything delays GTA 6, this drops fast. Hold and watch closely this week.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil headwinds building — consider your thesis
watch_today.detail: Banks including Goldman Sachs are cutting oil price forecasts following a US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough. Oil (WTI crude) is sitting at $75.39/barrel, down from $76.05. If the Iran deal holds, supply increases and energy stocks face a persistent headwind. FUEL.AX is already down 0.84% today. Your energy thesis may need a rethink if oil keeps drifting lower.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium bouncing — but watch for follow-through
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 2.75% today as spodumene prices tighten and the broader ASX lithium sector woke up. You're still sitting at a -5.64% loss overall on this position. Today's move is encouraging but you'd want to see a few more sessions of strength before reading too much into it. Hold for now.

watch_today.title: RBA holds at 4.35% — but warns rates could still go up
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank kept the official cash rate (the rate that flows through to your mortgage and savings) at 4.35% yesterday. The good news: no hike. The bad news: the RBA specifically flagged that future hikes are still on the table if inflation doesn't behave. No rate cuts are coming any time soon. Worth keeping in mind for any borrowing or fixed-rate decisions.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI tailwind strong, short-term dip is noise
watch_today.detail: Despite GXAI dipping 0.72% today, the AI backdrop is strengthening — Google, OpenAI and Anthropic were all at the G7 summit, and the US-Iran peace deal has removed a major uncertainty that was weighing on tech stocks. Your GXAI position is down 5% overall, but the medium-term case for AI infrastructure spending remains solid. Hold.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Valuation concerns creeping in — watch this week
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 1.48% last night and a detailed Seeking Alpha analysis argues its cash flow doesn't support its current price tag. You're already down 11.12% on this position. No immediate action needed, but it's worth watching whether MSFT finds support or continues sliding as the market reassesses big tech valuations.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid session today, closing up 0.54% at 8,966 points. Over in the US last night, it was a different story — the NASDAQ dropped 1.15% and the S&P 500 fell 0.57%, with tech stocks bearing most of the pain. Gold crept higher to $4,341/oz, oil slipped to $75.39/barrel on Iran deal news, and the Aussie dollar dipped slightly to around 70.6 US cents.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's US session — modest sell-off

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech took the brunt last night, down 1.15%

politics.summary: The big local story today is the RBA keeping rates on hold at 4.35% — welcome news for mortgage holders, but the central bank's warning about potential future hikes took the shine off it. Meanwhile, AI regulation is entering the Australian political conversation.

stories.title: RBA holds interest rates at 4.35% but warns hikes still possible
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia kept the official cash rate at 4.35% at its June meeting. That's the rate banks use to set your mortgage and savings rates, so no immediate change to repayments. However, the RBA's statement included what Nine.com.au called 'nine words no borrower wanted to see' — essentially a warning that further rate hikes remain on the table if inflation picks back up. No rate cuts are coming any time soon, so don't bank on mortgage relief in 2026.

stories.title: RBA delivers welcome relief — but also nine words no borrower wanted to see
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA's hold was broadly expected by economists, but the Board's language around 'not ruling out future increases' rattled some borrowers who were hoping for a softer tone. Variable rate mortgage holders can exhale for now, but the RBA is still watching inflation data closely. Any surprise jump in the next CPI (consumer price index — the official inflation measure) print could change the picture quickly.

stories.title: Pauline Hanson calls for AI regulation in Senate
stories.why_it_matters: One Nation senator Pauline Hanson used a Senate hearing to call for formal regulation of artificial intelligence in Australia, alongside questions about paid parental leave policy. It's early days, but AI regulation is now part of the Australian political debate — which matters for local tech and AI-exposed investments like GXAI.AX if rules start being drawn up.

ai.summary: AI is front and centre at the G7 summit today, with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google all in the room with world leaders. Meanwhile, a political battle in the US between the Trump administration and Anthropic is raising questions about America's long-term AI dominance — and who fills the gap if US policy gets messy.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google join Trump and world leaders at G7 AI summit
stories.why_it_matters: For the first time, the CEOs of OpenAI (Sam Altman), Anthropic, and Google sat alongside heads of state at the G7 summit. CNBC called it 'a signal of where power sits' — essentially, AI companies now have a seat at the table alongside elected governments when it comes to shaping global policy. For investors in GOOG or GXAI.AX, this signals that the biggest AI players are embedded at the highest levels of power, which is a long-term competitive moat.

stories.title: Trump's war on Anthropic threatens America's dominance of AI
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is reportedly in a running battle with Anthropic — one of the top two or three most important AI labs in the world — over regulation and government contracts. The Age and SMH argue this risks undermining America's lead in AI by creating uncertainty for the very companies pushing the frontier. If US policy makes life harder for Anthropic, it could inadvertently hand ground to Chinese competitors like DeepSeek. For GOOG holders, this is actually a slight positive — Google (as a more politically aligned player) could benefit.

stories.title: Business assessment: How OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini and Meta AI stack up
stories.why_it_matters: A detailed competitive analysis of the four major AI labs — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini and Meta AI — looks at where each sits commercially and technically. No article text available, but the key investment takeaway is that Google Gemini is increasingly competitive and Google's integration of AI across Search, Cloud and Workspace gives it structural advantages the pure-play AI labs lack. Relevant for GOOG and GXAI.AX holders.

stories.title: Stop copy-pasting prompts — this tool combines GPT-4o, Claude and Gemini for a one-time $55
stories.why_it_matters: A practical AI productivity tool is getting attention: a one-time $55 purchase lets you run prompts across GPT-4o (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic) and Gemini (Google) simultaneously, so you can compare responses without switching tabs. Not an investment story, but a useful tool if you're looking to get more out of AI in your day-to-day work without paying three separate subscriptions.

sport.summary: NRL Round 16 kicks off Friday with injury news dominating the build-up — Tom Trbojevic (Turbo) is back for the Sea Eagles, which is big. AFL has a Gather Round extension locked in for SA, and the Williams sisters are teaming up at Wimbledon.

stories.title: NRL Casualty Ward: Turbo back; Nicho Hynes and Robbie Brailey in frame for Round 16
stories.why_it_matters: Tom Trbojevic — 'Turbo', the Sea Eagles' star fullback — is confirmed back on deck for Round 16, which is a massive boost for Manly heading into Saturday's clash with the Bulldogs at Accor Stadium. Cronulla's Nicho Hynes and Newcastle's Robbie Brailey are also in the frame to return from injury. If you're playing NRL fantasy or tipping, Turbo's return changes the Sea Eagles' outlook significantly.

stories.title: NRL Round 16 team lists: Every club's confirmed lineup
stories.why_it_matters: Full confirmed team lists are out for Round 16. Key local game to watch: the Titans host the Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium on Saturday at 5:30pm — right in your backyard on the Gold Coast. Broncos, Eels and Rabbitohs are all on the bye this week.

stories.title: Roosters re-sign emerging forward; Duffy extends — 2026 NRL Signings Tracker
stories.why_it_matters: The Roosters have locked up an emerging forward and Tim Duffy has extended his deal — no full contract details in the article, but it signals Sydney are quietly building depth for a finals run. The signings tracker is worth bookmarking as the mid-season trade window starts heating up.

stories.title: Suns cult figure returns, Hawks star ruled out — AFL Team Tips Round 16
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Suns get back a cult figure this AFL round, while a Hawthorn star has been ruled out with injury ahead of this week's games. The article mentions a debut for a first-round pick too, which is always worth watching. No specific names available from the article text, but Fox Sports' team tips piece has the full breakdown.

stories.title: Williams sisters team up for Wimbledon doubles after 10 years
stories.why_it_matters: Serena and Venus Williams are teaming up for a Wimbledon doubles run — their first time partnering in 10 years. It's purely for fun (well, as much as anything the Williams sisters do is 'for fun'), and it'll be one of the most watched stories at this year's tournament. If you're a tennis fan, keep an eye on the draw.
